readingTexts.text:
NOTICE TO ALL STAFF

From Monday 3 March, the staff canteen will open at 11:30, not 12:00. The canteen will still close at 14:30.

We are making this change because many of you asked for an earlier lunch. The hot food counter will be open for the whole time, but the salad bar will only be ready from 12:00.

If you usually eat after 14:00, please note that the kitchen stops taking orders fifteen minutes before closing.

Questions? Speak to Mira in the office, or send an email. Please do not ask the kitchen staff during service.

Hi Dana,

Sorry for the late message. I can't come to the flat on Saturday after all — my sister is arriving from Almaty that morning and I have to meet her at the airport.

Could we do Sunday instead? I'm free any time before six. If Sunday doesn't work for you, I can come on Tuesday evening, but that's harder because I finish late.

I've still got your keys, so don't worry about that. I'll bring them either way.

Let me know what suits you.

Aigerim

When Timur started delivering food by bicycle, he assumed the hardest part would be the weather. In fact, he says, the weather was the easiest thing to plan for: you buy the right jacket and the problem is solved.

What he had not expected was how much of the job is waiting. Restaurants run late, customers do not answer their phones, and the app keeps counting the minutes as if the courier were responsible for all of it.

He still recommends the work to students, but with one condition. "Treat it as a job with bad hours, not as free time that happens to pay," he says. "People who think of it as flexible are the ones who end up working every evening."

From September, the city library will no longer charge fines for late returns. Instead, borrowers who keep a book for more than three weeks past the due date will simply be unable to borrow anything else until they bring it back.

The library says the change is not about being generous. Research from other cities suggests that fines mostly affect readers who were already struggling to visit regularly, while readers who could easily pay were never much deterred by them.

There is one exception. Items from the reference collection, which cannot normally leave the building, will keep their existing penalty, because a single missing volume can make a whole set useless.

Every few years a city announces that it has solved congestion, and every few years the solution turns out to have been a redistribution. Build a wider road and the traffic that was previously deterred by the journey time reappears to fill it; this is well documented enough to have its own name, and yet it continues to surprise the people who commission the roads.

What is less often said is that the same logic applies in the other direction. Remove a lane and some of the traffic does not divert — it evaporates. Trips that were marginal simply stop being made, or get made differently.

None of this makes lane removal automatically correct. It does mean that projections which assume a fixed quantity of traffic, to be pushed from one street to another, are describing a city that does not exist.

The premise of this book is that most organisational failure is not caused by bad decisions but by decisions nobody remembers making. It is a good premise, and the first hundred pages deliver on it with unusual precision: the case studies are specific, the interviews are recent, and the author resists the temptation to arrive at a single villain.

The second half is harder to defend. Having established that responsibility is usually diffuse, the author spends four chapters recommending interventions that assume a single person with the authority to implement them. The tension is never acknowledged, let alone resolved.

Readers looking for a diagnosis will find one of the best available. Readers looking for a cure should be warned that the prescription belongs to a different book.

A recurring difficulty in the literature is that the construct being measured shifts quietly between studies while the label stays the same. Two papers report on "engagement"; one operationalises it as time on task, the other as self-reported interest. Both are defensible choices. The problem arises only when a meta-analysis pools them, at which point the aggregate is a number about nothing in particular.

The conventional response is to demand tighter definitions in advance. That is reasonable, but it underestimates how much of the drift is invisible even to the researchers involved: a definition written in 2015 is read in 2024 through a decade of intervening usage.

A more tractable remedy is procedural rather than conceptual. If the instrument is reported in full, later readers can reconstruct what was actually measured, whatever the paper chose to call it.

There is a species of professional advice that survives not because it works but because failure is unattributable. Tell a hundred people to network relentlessly; the twenty who succeed will credit the advice, and the eighty who do not will conclude, with some encouragement from the literature, that they networked insufficiently. The counsel is thereby insulated from evidence in both directions.

What distinguishes genuinely useful guidance is not that it always works — nothing does — but that it specifies the conditions under which it should be abandoned. A recommendation with no failure mode attached is not a recommendation; it is a slogan with a bibliography.

This is worth saying because the slogans are not harmless. They occupy the attention that might otherwise be spent on advice narrow enough to be wrong.

lines.text: Last weekend I went to the market with my sister. We bought some fresh apples and a big fish. Then it started to rain so we took the bus home.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: I've been learning to cook for about a year now. At first I burned almost everything, but I didn't give up. Now I can make a few dishes my friends actually enjoy. Though I still can't bake a cake without checking the recipe twice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: What surprised me most about moving abroad wasn't the language. It was the silence. Back home, I was always surrounded by family and noise. Here the evenings can feel empty. I've had to learn that being alone is not the same as being lonely.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A good leader doesn't just give instructions. They create the conditions where people feel safe enough to take risks. The moment your team is more afraid of your reaction than of failure itself, innovation quietly dies.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Nostalgia is a curious thing. It dresses the past in colors it never actually wore. And yet we'd be poorer without it. We don't so much remember our lives as reinvent them. Each retelling smooths another rough edge, until the story we tell is kinder than the one we lived.

sources.summary: Ник и Анна: оба остались без планов, решают пойти в кино

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Hi, Nick! Are you waiting for someone?

lines.speaker: Nick
lines.text: Oh, hi Anna! Yes, I'm waiting for a friend, but he's just called and says he's not coming. We were going to the sports centre, but now I don't feel like going there alone.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Right, and I promised to meet my mum at the railway station. But she's missed her train and is coming on another one in three hours.

lines.speaker: Nick
lines.text: Which means you need to kill three hours somehow too, and it's rather cold and windy to stay in the street.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Right, I'm already starting to feel cold.

lines.speaker: Nick
lines.text: Look, I've heard there's an art exhibition in the art gallery, not far from here. How about going there together?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Oh no, art exhibitions are not for me, sorry. My alternative suggestion is going to the cinema, which is only two blocks from here. I don't remember the name of the film, but I've heard it's good.

lines.speaker: Nick
lines.text: Fine, let's go. I haven't been to the cinema for a very long time.

sources.summary: Профессии родителей Ника и мечты обоих о будущем

lines.speaker: Nick
lines.text: I haven't either. Last time it was more than three years ago, a family outing, so I couldn't escape to the stadium.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: It's strange you are so crazy about sports and do not like films. Your parents' careers are connected with the film industry somehow, aren't they?

lines.speaker: Nick
lines.text: Well, not exactly. My mum is a playwright — a person who writes texts for plays. And my dad is a cameraman. He shoots different programmes, interviews, concerts.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: I would like to work in the world of theatre and TV. It's so glamorous.

lines.speaker: Nick
lines.text: It's not very glamorous, in my opinion. The TV industry does not attract me at all. My ambition is more down to earth. I want to build bridges and buildings.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Architecture?

lines.speaker: Nick
lines.text: No, engineering. I think it's a very important profession.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: It is, but it's a difficult one. You need to know mathematics and science very well.

lines.speaker: Nick
lines.text: Yes, sure. I love mathematics more than any other subject.

lines.speaker: Nick
lines.text: Right, okay, as you say. And we've got to the place, I think.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Fine, but it looks sort of empty and deserted. Oh gosh, no.

lines.speaker: Nick
lines.text: What's wrong?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Look at this advertisement. It says that for some reason they have to cancel the films that start after 8 pm this weekend.

lines.speaker: Nick
lines.text: But Sunday was yesterday, wasn't it? And it's only 3 pm anyway. Why is it still closed?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Because it says here that on Monday and Tuesday there's nothing on at all. Come back on Wednesday.

lines.speaker: Nick
lines.text: Yeah, we need to switch to plan B, I suppose. Do we have one?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Hi, I'm Marco. I work in a small hotel near the station.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: I start at seven in the morning and I finish at three.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: I don't work on Sundays. On Sunday I usually visit my grandmother.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: My flat is very small.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: There is one bedroom, a kitchen and a bathroom.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: There isn't a garden, but there is a big window in the living room.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: I like it because it's near the park.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Excuse me, how much is this blue jacket?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: It's twenty-five pounds.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: And the black one?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: That one is cheaper. Nineteen pounds.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: OK. I'll take the black one, please.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: It's very cold today and it's raining.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: I can't go to the park with the children.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: So we are staying at home.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: We're watching a film and making pizza.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: Excuse me, is there a bank near here?

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Yes. Go straight and then turn right at the hospital.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: The bank is next to a small coffee shop.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: Thank you very much.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: This is a photo of my family.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: My mother is a teacher and my father works in a shop.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: I have got one sister. She is eleven.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: We have got a big dog. His name is Rocky.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Attention passengers. The four fifteen service to Leeds will now leave from platform six, not platform two.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: The train is running about ten minutes late because of engineering work.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Passengers travelling to Manchester should change at Leeds.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Last summer we went camping in the mountains.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: The first two days were terrible. It rained all the time and we couldn't cook outside.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: But then the weather changed and the last three days were really beautiful.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: I definitely want to go back next year.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Hi Daniel, it's Karen from the office.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: The meeting on Wednesday has moved to Thursday, same time, same room.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Could you bring the printed reports? Sam won't be there, so we'll need your numbers.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Call me back if that's a problem.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Are you free on Saturday afternoon?

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: Saturday's difficult. I'm helping my brother move house.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Sunday then? There's a new exhibition at the gallery.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: Sunday works. What time does it open?

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Ten, but let's meet at eleven. It's quieter later.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: My sister is a photographer, but she doesn't work in a studio.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: She travels to different cities and takes pictures of buildings.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: It's hard work because she's away from home a lot.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: But she says she wouldn't change it.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Should we take the bus or the train to the airport?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: The bus is cheaper, about half the price.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: But how long does it take?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Nearly two hours. The train's only forty minutes.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Let's pay more. I don't want to miss the flight.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: So how's the new job going?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Yeah, good. Better than I expected, actually. The work itself is fine.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: But?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Well, the commute. It's an hour and a half each way.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Could you move closer?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: I did look into it, but the rents round there are ridiculous. So I asked about working from home two days a week.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: And they agreed?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Starting next month, yeah.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: I'm thinking of joining the gym on Mill Street.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: The one with the pool? I went there for about six months.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: Was it any good?

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: The equipment's excellent. But it gets really crowded after five, and that's the only time I could go.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: I'd be going in the mornings, though.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Then honestly, you'd probably love it.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Hi, I'd like to book the photography course starting in March.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: Certainly. The full course is two hundred and forty pounds.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Is there a student discount?

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: There is, but it's already closed for March. It'll be available again for the April course.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Then I'll wait for April. Can you hold a place?

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: I can, for a week.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Excuse me, my suitcase didn't come through with the others.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: I'm sorry about that. Could you describe it?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Medium size, dark green, with a red label on the handle.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Right. We had a bag arrive on the wrong flight this morning. Was yours coming from Dublin?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: No, Edinburgh.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Then that's not it, I'm afraid. Let me take your details and we'll deliver it as soon as it turns up.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Have you seen that documentary everyone's talking about?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: I watched it last weekend. It's beautifully filmed, I'll give it that.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: You don't sound convinced.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: It's just very long. Two and a half hours, and the middle section drags badly.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: So would you recommend it?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: If you're interested in the subject, definitely. If not, probably not.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: I booked a room with a balcony, but the one I've been given doesn't have one.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: Let me check. Ah, I see. The balcony rooms are all occupied tonight.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: That's not really my problem, is it?

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: No, you're right. I can move you tomorrow morning, or refund the difference now.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: I'd rather not pack everything again. Let's do the refund.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Right, so we've had the survey results back on the hybrid policy.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: Let me guess. Everyone wants to stay at home.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Actually, no. Sixty per cent said they'd come in more often if the office were less noisy.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: Huh. That's not what I expected at all.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Which suggests the problem was never really the commute.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: I'd still be careful reading too much into it. Sixty per cent said that, but only a third actually filled the survey in.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Fair point. Though it's the closest thing to evidence we've got.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: You spent twelve years in corporate law before switching to teaching. What prompted that?

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: People always assume there was some dramatic moment. There wasn't.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: It was more that I kept noticing which parts of the week I looked forward to, and none of them involved the actual law.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Was money not a concern?

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Of course it was. I'd be lying if I said otherwise. But I'd also saved for six years knowing something would change eventually.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: So it was planned.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Planned is generous. Anticipated, maybe.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: We're three weeks behind on the launch and I need to know why.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: The short answer is the payments integration.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: And the long answer?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: The long answer is that we knew in January it would be tight, and we scoped it as if it wouldn't be.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: So it's a planning problem, not an engineering one.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: I'd say both. But if you're asking which one we can fix before the next launch, then yes, planning.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: All right. That's more useful than I was expecting.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: What did you think of the second candidate?

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Technically strong. Probably the strongest we've seen.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: I sense a "but".

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: She talked about her last team for twenty minutes and used "I" every single time.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: That might just be interview nerves. People oversell themselves under pressure.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: It might. I'd want a second conversation before I decided either way.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: That seems reasonable.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Your book argues that screen time is basically a meaningless measure. That's quite a claim.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: It's a deliberately provocative way of putting it, but yes.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Two hours spent video-calling your grandmother and two hours scrolling in bed at midnight are not the same thing, and yet we count them identically.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Critics would say you're downplaying a genuine problem.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Some do, and I understand why. My point isn't that nothing is wrong. It's that we're measuring the wrong variable and then acting surprised when the interventions don't work.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Before we move on, I wanted to raise something about the sampling.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: You've recruited entirely through the university's own mailing list, which is efficient, obviously. But it does mean your sample is drawn from people who already engage with institutional communication.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: That's a fair observation. Though I'd note the effect sizes are large enough that a modest selection bias wouldn't overturn the direction of the finding.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: I'm not suggesting it would. I'm suggesting the magnitude is probably inflated, and the paper currently reads as though it isn't.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: That's a reasonable distinction. I'd be happy to soften the framing in the discussion section.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: The council's position is that pedestrianising the centre will increase footfall for local businesses.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: And in most comparable cities it has. What tends to get left out is the timeline.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: Footfall recovers, yes, but typically after eighteen months to two years, and a lot of independent retailers simply don't have that runway.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: So you'd oppose the scheme.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: No, I'd sequence it differently. Support first, restriction second. Doing them in the opposite order is how you end up with an empty pedestrian zone and a very unpopular council.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Are we heading for a recession or not?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: I'd resist the framing, if you don't mind.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: The indicators that historically preceded contractions are behaving unusually this cycle. Employment is holding in a way it typically doesn't, and consumer spending has stayed resilient longer than most of us forecast.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: That sounds like a no.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: It sounds like a "the model that would tell us is currently not working". Which is a less satisfying answer, but a more honest one.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: I wanted to talk about the client presentation on Thursday.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: Sure. I thought it landed reasonably well.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: The content was strong. Genuinely. The analysis was the best work you've done here.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: I'm sensing there's more.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: There were about forty slides for a fifty-minute slot, and we got through nineteen. The client saw a fifth of your argument and none of your conclusion.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: Right. So the problem wasn't what I said, it's what they never got to hear.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: That's exactly it.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Every technology introduced into classrooms in the last forty years was going to transform learning, and none of them did.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: I'd accept that for interactive whiteboards. I'm less sure it holds here.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: The earlier tools changed how material was delivered. They didn't change who could give a student individual attention at the moment they were stuck.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Assuming the attention is any good.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Assuming that, yes. Which is an empirical question rather than a reason to dismiss it in advance.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Then we agree on the question. We just disagree about how confident anyone should be about the answer.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: So the piece came in at four thousand words.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: Against a brief of eighteen hundred.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Against a brief of eighteen hundred, yes.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: In fairness, it's four thousand rather good words.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Nobody's disputing that. I'm disputing the arithmetic.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: I suppose what I'm asking is whether we cut it or find it more room.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: We could find it more room. We'd just be finding it at the expense of something else, and I notice nobody's volunteering their own copy.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: That does tend to be how it works.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: The headline finding has been picked up more or less everywhere.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: It has, which is the part I find difficult.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: The paper says the association holds within a narrowly defined subgroup and explicitly declines to generalise. The coverage says the opposite, and cites the paper.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Are the authors pushing back?

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Not conspicuously.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Well. There are worse things than being famous for something you didn't quite claim.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: There are. Though I'd have thought a correction was cheaper than the reputation of a whole subfield.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: So, the new production. Ambitious?

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Ambitious is the word everyone reaches for, and it's doing a great deal of work in this case.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: Meaning?

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Meaning the staging is genuinely inventive, the design is beautiful, and roughly forty minutes in it becomes apparent that nobody involved has decided what the play is about.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: That's rather harsh.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Is it? I'd say it's harsher to pretend a production is finished when what you've seen is a very expensive rehearsal.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: And yet you'd recommend it.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: I'd recommend seeing it. I wouldn't recommend paying full price.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: I'll grant you the policy was badly communicated.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Badly communicated, poorly timed, and announced by someone who plainly hadn't read it.

lines.speaker: M_US
lines.text: I feel the concession slipping away.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: It is, slightly. Because none of that touches whether the policy itself was right, and the entire debate since has been about the announcement.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: That's often how it goes, though. If you can't win on substance, you litigate the process.

lines.speaker: F_GB
lines.text: Which would be a fair characterisation if anyone had actually tried to win on substance first.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Will you be standing for the leadership?

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: I'm focused entirely on the work in front of me.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: That isn't a no.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: It isn't a yes either.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: With respect, you've given that answer four times this month, and the question keeps getting asked because the answer keeps not being one.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Then perhaps we should both consider what that tells us about the question.

lines.speaker: M_GB
lines.text: Or about the answer.

lines.speaker: F_US
lines.text: Or about the answer, yes.
